edit.description: `normalize_lf` (:2527) is a second EOL normalizer — same rule as `hash::canonicalize_eol` (CRLF collapses to one LF, a lone CR becomes LF), written over chars instead of bytes, with its own doc restating the same contract. One call site: the render closure in `emit_one` (:2621). Delete the function and call the shared surface there.

The module header already names itself the home of `canonicalize_eol`. Give the byte implementation (:27) a `&str` face the projection writer can call without a bytes round-trip (CR is ASCII, so canonicalizing UTF-8 bytes can never break the encoding — state that at the site), and pin the rule in a unit test the module currently has none of.

summary: `drift::normalize_lf` is a second EOL normalizer beside `hash::canonicalize_eol` — one job, two homes; fold its single call site onto the shared surface.

tests.asserts: The shared EOL surface collapses CRLF to one LF, maps a lone CR to LF, leaves an already-LF text byte-identical, and preserves multi-byte UTF-8 either side of a CR — the rule `normalize_lf` carried privately, now pinned in its one home.
The existing CRLF-bearing emit cases still project LF-uniform bytes, so the fold moves no projection byte.

acceptance: `cargo test` green with `normalize_lf` gone from src/drift.rs and the EOL rule pinned in src/hash.rs; `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.
